semantics: Refactor candidates that were investigated, costed and refused, as data rather than prose. The format is section 2 of .agents/docs/implemented/process/2026-09-20-agent-refactorability-gates.md; the ratchet suite that note describes has since been removed. Each candidate carries an `id`, the `symbols` that carry its shape, and a `ruling` anchor holding the evidence. Each symbol's `signature` records the declaration as it stood when the candidate was refused (bodies elided as `{…}`, comments stripped, whitespace collapsed). No test checks it: a symbol whose shape has since changed is a cue to re-read the ruling, and the PR that changes the shape updates the entry. Citing the candidate's `id` in the PR body is a convention, not checked. Re-proposing a refused candidate as originally specified is the failure this exists to stop; landing a candidate on NEW evidence is legal, and that PR cites the id, states what changed, and deletes or rewrites the entry.

candidates.candidate: the platform config providers onto an Effect ConfigProvider
candidates.why: Config<T> over the platform port's own get buys nothing: the read stays synchronous and answers for the workspace the caller was handed. Naming each row a second time as Config.Boolean/Config.Int beside the Zod catalog row that owns it is a dual schema system with a ConfigError where Settings.get's validation already stands. Settings stay synchronous by ruling; Effect Config is for process.env reads, a separate lane.

candidates.candidate: withPerKeyLane onto an Effect Semaphore
candidates.why: Re-checked on Effect 4.1.0. Semaphore no longer barges (4.0.7), but take, takeScoped and withPermit are Effects that join its queue one evaluation after refuseClaim decides, and the fiber can yield in between (Scheduler.shouldYield at MaxOpsBeforeYield, 2048 by default), so a fiber that claimed later enters first: a one-permit Semaphore per lane did so at 2 of 2101 claim offsets at the default budget and in about half of 150 six-fiber runs at budgets 8 and 13, the Deferred chain never. The chain swaps its tail in the step that runs refuseClaim, which RunRegistry's admission relies on. An RcMap of semaphores would own the lane map each caller passes (RunRegistry keeps its lanes on its run entries, two callers key a WeakMap), needs a Scope to build, and answers get as an Effect, so refuseClaim could not read the occupant in the claim step. The lane maps prune themselves, so making them services is a pure net-add.

candidates.candidate: ModelRetryGate onto the effect/persistence CircuitBreaker, with Effect.retry on its rejections behind the unchanged withRoutes
candidates.why: The breaker cannot keep the gate's backoff rule. Its opening count survives a close and resets only by time, once the circuit has stayed closed as long as it was last open (node_modules/effect/src/persistence/CircuitBreaker.ts:15-16, :1143-1146, :1195, effect 4.1.0); a success while closed clears only the trip streak (:1204), and the next opening counts from the count the failing call started under (:480). The gate ends its streak on the first clean round-trip of a healthy route and never on a probe success (`settle` in packages/harness/src/agent/runtime/ModelRetryGate.ts, from #9078 and kept by #14781), so a released herd that fails at once grows the backoff while a route failing between successes stays at the base. Measured with one clean success between each recovery and the next failure: the gate cooled 1000 ms seven times; the breaker (jittered exponential from 1 s, capped at 5 min, midpoint jitter) opened for 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000 and 64000 ms. Every 5xx, 408 and 429 not scoped to the model cools the whole wire route (packages/llm/src/errors.ts:155-156), so an intermittently overloaded provider would stall every run on that credential toward the 5-minute cap; a constant openDuration brings back the herd re-failing at the base backoff that #9078 fixed. The breaker also never waits (CircuitBreaker.ts:18-21, :1149-1162) and withRoutes cannot add an error, so it would poll for as long as the probe runs, a whole billed turn (`ModelInvoker.invoke`), where a cooling route's callers wait out the backoff, one goes through as the probe, and the rest go with it once the route opens (`through` in ModelRetryGate.ts). classify has seen whether the call is the probe since effect 4.1.1 ({ probe }), which answers none of the reasons above; openDuration is fixed per breaker (:452-457) where baseBackoffMs is per call; the module is @stability experimental (:121).

candidates.candidate: The stdio MCP client (mcpServer.ts over jsonRpc.ts newline framing) onto effect/ai McpClient.stdio
candidates.why: effect 4.1.0's McpClient (@stability experimental) speaks one protocol revision per client and fails any other answer: its ProtocolVersion is 2025-11-25 | 2026-07-28 (node_modules/effect/src/ai/McpClient.ts:66, :541-545), it sends initialize once (:283-290), and a server answering another revision fails with UnsupportedError (:305-308). A server that does not speak the requested revision answers with its own latest (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.0 dist/esm/server/index.js:259-263), so every stdio server still on 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 or 2024-11-05 would start with no tools; ours asks for 2025-06-18 and accepts whatever the server answers (packages/harness/src/tools/mcp/mcpServer.ts:50, :334-342). Its decoding also rejects shapes ours accepts: a null optional field or a tool without inputSchema.type fails the whole tools/list (ai/internal/mcpSchema/v2024_11_05.ts:23-31, v2025_06_18.ts:218-234), and an unknown content block fails the call (v2025_06_18.ts:243-248). Adoption would delete about 135 lines and bring notifications/cancelled on interrupt (McpClient.ts:655-661); mcpConfig.ts has no counterpart. Revisit when McpClient accepts an older revision in the server's answer.

candidates.why: Two layers, not two copies. SessionViewService is the view updater: the session's own view and the cross-process RemoteSessionView (which has no store) are both built on it. candidates.why: The lane guards a root's .lake directory, which outlives any one server: restart_server and stop_server drop a root's server from the pool's LayerMap and start a new one while a build still holds a lease on the old one, so a semaphore owned by the server would let the new server's build run beside the old one's. candidates.candidate: GitHub subscriptions as an RcMap keyed by target, with a PubSub per entry each binding consumes through Stream.fromPubSub, and the poll fiber forked in the entry's scope
candidates.why: Three facts the design does not survive. (1) A processLayer may require only PluginLayerServices (packages/harness/src/tools/toolTable.ts), which lack Secrets and HttpClient, so an RcMap made there cannot type a lookup that starts the poll; RcMap merges the getter's context into the lookup at run time (node_modules/effect/dist/RcMap.js get), so it would work only behind a cast that hides the requirement. (2) The run bindings are needed anyway (list, unbind, unbindAll, the per-run annotation level), so the RcMap's reference count would be a second count of the same fact; a target that ends itself (a closed PR, a rejected token) then has to leave both, and RcMap.invalidate plus releases from another fiber leave a window where a new bind reuses the dying entry, whose FiberHandle still holds the finishing poller. (3) A PubSub subscriber takes events on its own fiber, so an event published but not yet taken is outside the FiberSet the shutdown drain awaits, and is lost at shutdown. What landed instead: one Map from target path to its runs, the poll fibers in one FiberMap keyed by the same path (the last unbind removes the key; a poller that ends removes its subscription in its own step), and deliveries forked into one FiberSet at publish time.

symbols.signature: export const gitHubSubscriptionsLayer: Layer.Layer< GitHubSubscriptions, never, AppSignals > = Layer.effect(…);

candidates.candidate: the desktop window as one FiberHandle: open as FiberHandle.run with onlyIfMissing, the closed event as FiberHandle.clear, the shutdown as awaitEmpty, the quit's resume as a Deferred
candidates.why: FiberHandle.run with onlyIfMissing returns an already-interrupted fiber while the handle still holds the closing window's fiber (FiberHandle.js runImpl), and clear holds it there until the window's scope has released. A reopen asked for during a close (the macOS dock click right after closing) would be dropped instead of waiting for the release and opening, which the current open does with `releasing`. awaitEmpty before run cannot replace it: on an open window it never returns, so open would need the closing state again. The quit's resume must also stay on setImmediate: a quit requested from inside `closed` lands before Electron removes the window and is abandoned. What remains is the three optionals as one state value (closed, open, closing), not a different primitive.

symbols.signature: export function createDesktopWindows(options: {…}): DesktopWindows {…}

candidates.candidate: the run listing entry carries RunView.actions (runActions) in place of resumable/resumeBlocked, so listRuns stops calling deriveResumability
candidates.why: The two answer different questions. The listing's resumable is deriveResumability's checkpoint: a run that continues from its rows whatever its outcome, so a completed conversation is listed resumable and the CLI resume list enables it, and resumeBlocked carries why rows cannot be continued here (an earlier build, damaged rows, a plugin this process does not load). runActions offers resume only on an interrupted loop-driven run or an unfinished script, and reads the view, which holds no plugin facts, so the listing would disable every finished conversation and lose the blocked reason (packages/harness/example/10-external-plugin.ts asserts it). continuesFromRows is the shared rule both read on purpose, not a second decider.

candidates.candidate: the user's Accept-time edit recorded on the document task's own run: the revision record gains `userEdit: { round, diff } | null`, written by the progress view's Accept (ProgressWorkflowFileActionsController.userEdit), and document_context reads it into the next revision's prompt
candidates.why: No supported write reaches the run's documents fact from the host's Accept path. A run's `plugin.fact` rows are committed only by the run's own tool calls (`ToolResult.facts`, in the call's `tool.result` batch); the one other plugin write, `RequestDecisionHook.commit`, runs only while a pending plugin request of the run is being decided and commits facts about the plugin's own aggregate (`ownFactRow` hangs them under the run as `plugin:<aggregate>`), which `RunView.facts` and `documentRoundsOf` never read. A host-side append to an ended run would be a new session-store write path in the harness. It would also have no reader: Accept acts on outputs the task already proposed, a completed recipe does not run another revision on resume, a fork drops the documents fact (`fork: 'drop'`), and Run again is a new run with fresh documents. An Accept while the task still runs would race the recipe's whole-list commit (`withRound`), which drops the other writer's change. The launcher note #14713 sends (`followUpLauncher`) is the reader that exists; a task with no launcher has no later turn to read the edit.
